tags.name: page
tags.description: Serves the single page the Vue app boots from. Everything the page then does goes through the API controllers, so this class stays free of app logic.

tags.name: vehicle
tags.description: The vehicle routes the web UI uses. Every rule lives in VehicleService, so what happens here is the translation between a request and an answer (docs/adr/0006-one-api-surface-in-v1.md).

tags.name: odometer
tags.description: The readings that hang off one vehicle. Every rule lives in OdometerService (docs/architecture.md#odometer-rules), including the access check.

tags.name: trip
tags.description: The trips that hang off one vehicle. Every rule lives in TripService, including the access check.

tags.name: energy
tags.description: The fill-ups and charging sessions that hang off one vehicle. Every rule lives in EnergyService, including the access check.

tags.name: maintenance
tags.description: The Maintenance Records that hang off one vehicle. Every rule lives in MaintenanceService, including the access check.

tags.name: expense
tags.description: The Expenses that hang off one vehicle. Every rule lives in ExpenseService, including the access check.

tags.name: reminder
tags.description: The reminders that hang off one vehicle. Every rule lives in ReminderService, including the access check.

tags.name: recipient
tags.description: Who one vehicle's reminders go to. Every rule lives in RecipientService, including the access check. Each route answers with the list as it now stands, so there is no token: adding and removing one person commute.

tags.name: grant
tags.description: Who else may use one vehicle. Every rule lives in GrantService, the access check included. Each route answers with the list as it now stands, and there is no token for the reason RecipientController gives: only the owner writes it, and each write names its grantee.

tags.name: document
tags.description: One vehicle's papers. Every rule lives in DocumentService, including the access check. Each route answers with the list as it now stands, so there is no token: nothing edits a document.

tags.name: booking
tags.description: The bookings that hang off one vehicle. Every rule lives in BookingService, including the access check.

tags.name: timeline
tags.description: The one timeline a vehicle has. Every rule lives in TimelineService, including the access check.

tags.name: kpi
tags.description: The figures in a vehicle's header and on its Costs screen. Every rule lives in KpiService, including the access check.

tags.name: report
tags.description: Printable pages the browser turns into paper (docs/adr/0005-no-pdf-library.md), and the CSV files beside them. What is in them is the services'; this serves them.

tags.name: preferences
tags.description: The personal settings screen's two calls. Like every other controller here it carries no rules (docs/adr/0006-one-api-surface-in-v1.md); a preference carries no `updated_at` either, because a user's own setting has no second writer to lose a race against.

tags.name: inbox
tags.description: The Inbox screen's one read. Choosing the folder is a preference (PreferencesController), so nothing here writes.

tags.name: ocs_vehicle
tags.description: The vehicles through the OCS door: the twin of the internal VehicleController, over the same service calls (docs/api.md).

tags.name: ocs_odometer
tags.description: A vehicle's Readings through the OCS door: the twin of the internal OdometerController (docs/api.md, docs/architecture.md#odometer-rules).

tags.name: ocs_trip
tags.description: A vehicle's trips through the OCS door: the twin of the internal TripController (docs/api.md).

tags.name: ocs_energy
tags.description: A vehicle's fill-ups and charging sessions through the OCS door: the twin of the internal EnergyController (docs/api.md).

tags.name: ocs_maintenance
tags.description: A vehicle's Maintenance Records through the OCS door: the twin of the internal MaintenanceController (docs/api.md).

tags.name: ocs_expense
tags.description: A vehicle's Expenses through the OCS door: the twin of the internal ExpenseController (docs/api.md).

tags.name: ocs_timeline
tags.description: A vehicle's one timeline through the OCS door: the twin of the internal TimelineController (docs/api.md, docs/architecture.md#the-timeline).

tags.name: ocs_kpi
tags.description: A vehicle's figures through the OCS door: the twin of the internal KpiController (docs/api.md, docs/architecture.md#numbers-consumption-cost-emissions).

tags.name: ocs_reminder
tags.description: A vehicle's reminders through the OCS door: the twin of the internal ReminderController (docs/api.md). Their state is the engine's (docs/architecture.md#reminder-engine), so no write here sets it.

tags.name: ocs_recipient
tags.description: Who one vehicle's reminders go to, through the OCS door: the twin of the internal RecipientController (docs/api.md). Each answer is the list as it now stands, and no write carries a token, for the reason the twin gives. A write still maps every refusal the twin maps, a 412 included, so the two doors cannot answer one failure differently.

tags.name: ocs_grant
tags.description: Who else may use one vehicle, through the OCS door: the twin of the internal GrantController (docs/api.md). The owner reads and writes the list; a grantee reads and leaves their own access. Each answer is what the caller now holds or the list as it now stands, and no write carries a token, for the reason the twin gives; a 412 is still answered as the twin answers it (RecipientController).

tags.name: ocs_document
tags.description: One vehicle's papers through the OCS door: the twin of the internal DocumentController, all but the download, which stays a link (docs/api.md#downloads). Each answer is the list as it now stands, and no write carries a token, for the reason the twin gives; a 412 is still answered as the twin answers it (RecipientController).

tags.name: ocs_booking
tags.description: A vehicle's bookings and their handover through the OCS door: the twin of the internal BookingController (docs/api.md).

tags.name: ocs_preferences
tags.description: The caller's own settings through the OCS door: the twin of the internal PreferencesController (docs/api.md). No token, for the reason the twin gives.

tags.name: ocs_inbox
tags.description: What waits in the caller's inbox folder, through the OCS door: the twin of the internal InboxController (docs/api.md). The folder is a preference, so nothing here writes.

tags.name: ocs_sync
tags.description: What changed for a client since its last call (docs/api.md#sync). The one OCS route with no internal twin: the web UI reads what is on screen, and keeps nothing to bring up to date.
